claims.head: A shadow job for Smith, Frondell and Teräväinen
claims.call: The Blackhawks’ L3 (Smith, Frondell and Teräväinen) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Blue Jackets’ first line, against about 36% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Frondell’s line (Smith, Frondell and Teräväinen) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Blue Jackets’ first line is Knies, Bel Belluz and Johnson.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 2 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Valeri Nichushkin takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Erik Gudbranson is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Provorov and Christiansen.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Conor Garland has not dressed for the last 4 games.
Sean Monahan is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 30% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 126:21 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Connor Bedard is out (shoulder injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blackhawks (6-13-2) beat Toronto 6-3 on Tuesday, while the Blue Jackets are on a five-game losing streak. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Blue Jackets are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th in the NHL) and the Hawks last in the Central (tied for 29th).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.368) says: their chances are worth about .485, and their finishing has held them back. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.333) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .389, and their goaltending has held them back.
In their five-game skid, the Blue Jackets have been outscored 21-8, including 14-6 at 5-on-5.

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (2nd) and do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest). They also forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), so the Blue Jackets hound the puck, but the Blackhawks sit back. Columbus has scored 2.32 goals a game, the fewest in the league. On the other side, the Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest), don’t block many shots (32nd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). Chicago has scored 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league, and allowed 4.05, the second most.

Kent Johnson (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 19 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring. Zach Werenski (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind, with a point in six straight games against Chicago. Frank Nazar (10 G / 2 A / 12 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Blackhawks’ scoring lead. Roman Kantserov (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 21 GP) shares it.
Cam Talbot (5-4-0 / .906 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Columbus, and Spencer Knight (6-10-1 / .884 SV% in 17 GS) for Chicago.
At home, Jeff Blashill likes to send Smith, Frondell and Teräväinen out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Knies, Bel Belluz and Johnson.
